stage1.impression: A moody, warm, coherent night interior with good composition down the counter, and the blurred figures add life. But it reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The oak slats, plaster and table tops are clean and uniform. The lit band under the ceiling reads as a flat gold lightbox, not cast acrylic fins. The hero speaker is a tiny red sliver half hidden behind the porch door, and a multicolour neon ring sculpture beside it outshouts it. A magazine would see a well-lit generic bar, not a specific place: the lantern idea is there, but the frame does not sell it.

blocking_9: The Tropos speaker must read at a glance as the hero: visible whole (or at least its full face) through the porch, its region lum_median >= 45, its Ember tint legible
The acrylic band must read as thick, smoked cast fins with glowing polished edges and fin-to-fin depth, not a flat, evenly lit gold panel at lum ~132 that is the brightest large surface in the frame
The bar top must carry real pools of light from the counter spots (quartzite and glasses legible); it is now lum_median ~25
The right plaster wall (about 21% of the frame) must stop being a dead brown void: it needs a graze or falloff that shows lime plaster texture
Surfaces need photographic irregularity at 1:1: oak tone variation slat to slat, plaster trowel marks, wear on the tables; no fireflies or CG haze shafts
Only one saturated colour source: the multicolour neon rings compete with the speaker

defects.what: Hero speaker is about 30 x 90 px, cut by the porch door leaf, lum_median 29.4, reads as a red box rather than a tinted acrylic speaker
Multicolour neon rings (blue, green, yellow, red) are the most saturated thing in the frame and draw the eye from the speaker
Acrylic band reads as a flat matte gold board/lightbox; fins barely resolve, no edge glow, lum_median 131.9 makes it the dominant bright mass
Fireflies: isolated white specks on the band at about (713,212) and (790,222)
A diagonal volumetric light shaft from the upper left that comes from no visible source; reads as CG haze
Hot spot on the baffle under the band from the graze/downlight, slightly harsh
Bar top underlit (lum_median 25.1); no pools of light on the quartzite despite 4 counter spots
Large flat, untextured dark plaster wall (lum_median 19.2) with no light on it; dead area
Oak slats are perfectly uniform in tone and spacing; CG-clean
Identical black table tops with no wear, reflection or props variety; read as repeated copies
Foreground terrazzo counter face and floor at the lower left are murky (lum_median 14.3)
Ceiling downlights show as bare white dots on a black void ceiling; ceiling texture unreadable (lum_median 13.1)

changes.problem: The hero speaker is tiny and half hidden behind the porch door leaf, so the frame has no clear subject.

evidence.measured: speaker visible over about 30 x 90 px; the door leaf at x 600-700 hides the rest

change.to: about [5.2, 3.3, 1.40] looking at [13.0, 3.9, 1.6], 32 mm, so the porch opening frames the Tropos face and Mother falls behind the door or out of the opening

changes.expected: The speaker's full front reads through the porch at about 3 to 4 times its current area, in the central third; the neon rings are mostly cropped by the door leaf.

changes.problem: The speaker is underlit, so its Ember tint and the light through its acrylic do not read.

evidence.measured: lum_median 29.4 (target >= 45), r/g/b median 54/23/12, delta-E 30 vs a mid ember #C0401A

change.setting: inside the lantern: the pair spots
change.to: 2 x 110 W, 20 deg, aimed at the speakers' tops and backs so light passes through the acrylic

changes.expected: The speaker glows warm orange, the brightest saturated thing in the frame; region lum_median 50 to 80.

changes.problem: Mother EARF's multicolour rings compete with the speaker as a second saturated colour source.

evidence.measured: saturated blue, green, yellow and red lines, visually more saturated than the speaker

change.setting: inside the lantern: Mother EARF spot
change.to: 25 W, 16 deg (and let c1's camera place her behind the door leaf)

changes.expected: The rings fall to a dim accent, or out of frame; the speaker is the only saturated colour.

changes.problem: The acrylic band reads as a flat gold lightbox and is the brightest large mass, pulling the eye up and away from the speaker.

evidence.measured: lum_median 131.9, x falloff flat (122 to 142 across the band), fins barely resolved

change.to: 0.06, with the emitter set back behind the fins so each fin's polished edge catches light and the gaps fall darker

changes.expected: The band reads as smoked amber fins with glowing edges and a rhythm of light and dark; lum_median about 70 to 100.

changes.problem: The bar top has no pools of light, so the quartzite, the glasses and the counter's length do not read.

change.to: 4 x 70 W, 22 deg, aimed at the top's front edge with a pool every 1.2 m

changes.expected: Distinct pools on the quartzite with darker gaps between them; the glasses get highlights.

changes.problem: The right plaster wall is a large, dead, untextured dark area.

evidence.measured: lum_median 19.2, lum_range 59; no gradient or texture

change.to: 4 x 22 W, 30 deg, tilted 10 deg toward the wall so they scallop the lime plaster above the banquette

changes.expected: Soft scallops of warm light on the plaster with trowel texture showing, fading to dark at the ceiling; region lum_median about 28 to 40.

changes.problem: Fireflies on the band and a sourceless diagonal haze shaft read as render artifacts.

evidence.measured: white specks at about (713,212) and (790,222); the diagonal shaft at 420-540, 130-230

change.to: clamp 4, haze 0.004/m, and aim or cut the downlight that makes the shaft (or occlude it so the shaft falls from a visible fixture)

changes.expected: No isolated specks on the band; haze is only a faint glow around the practicals.

changes.problem: The oak slats, plaster and table tops are uniformly clean and read as CG at 1:1.

evidence.measured: slat tone near constant; lum_range 98 comes from the lighting, not the material

change.setting: the oak's tone and the plaster's tone (finish within kind)
change.to: per-slat tone variation of +/-8 %, visible grain and slight oil sheen; plaster with trowel mottling; table tops with faint rings and wear, and props varied per table (a record sleeve, a coat, different glasses)

changes.expected: The surfaces read as real oiled oak and lime plaster at 1:1, and the tables stop reading as copies.

out_of_scope.request: Make the speaker larger or move it toward the porch so it reads from the bar room
out_of_scope.why: EARF's products and the lantern's plan are fixed as placed; only the camera and light can bring it forward

out_of_scope.request: Tone Mother EARF's rings down to one colour
out_of_scope.why: The product's colours are fixed; only its spot and the camera may change

out_of_scope.request: Remove the porch door leaf that hides the speaker
